headline: Scientists find air around a faraway planet

sources.title: Potential Atmosphere Detected on Habitable-Zone Exoplanet LHS 1140b
Astronomers spot first atmosphere around a potentially habitable alien world
Rocky Planet 48 Light-Years Away May Be First in a Habitable Zone With a Confirmed Atmosphere

chunks.text: For the first time ever, scientists have {{picked up}} signs of air around a small, rocky planet far from Earth. The planet is called LHS 1140 b, and it sits about 48 [[light-years]] away. It moves around its star in the [[habitable zone]], the area where the temperature could be just right for water. Finding air around such a planet is a big deal, because a planet needs air to {{hold on to}} heat and to protect any life. But this discovery soon {{turned into}} a real mystery.

chunks.text: LHS 1140 b is what scientists call a [[super-Earth]], which means it is rocky like Earth but much bigger. It goes around a small, cool red star. To study it, a team from Harvard University {{set out}} to watch the planet with a powerful [[telescope]] in Chile. In 2024, the telescope {{came across}} [[helium]] gas leaking from the top of the planet's air and floating out into space. Because the star {{gives off}} strong [[radiation]], it slowly {{strips away}} this gas.

chunks.text: Here is where the mystery {{comes in}}. When the same team {{went back}} to check their work in 2025, the helium signal had completely disappeared. One scientist said it was a rare chance to watch the air of a faraway planet change in such a short time. In other words, the planet's air may be changing in ways we can actually see. Still, the researchers are careful. They cannot be sure yet, and more work is needed to {{figure out}} what is really {{going on}}.

chunks.text: To clear things up, the team will soon {{carry out}} new studies with the James Webb Space Telescope, the most powerful space telescope ever built. Their main goal is to {{track down}} water, which would prove the air is real and [[stable]]. If they can {{pull off}} this hard task, LHS 1140 b could become one of the best places to search for life beyond Earth. And that brings us a little closer to a question people have asked for thousands of years: are we alone?
